function: DRL (ACDRL/HDCDRL) learns AAV trajectory, OFDMA subchannel allocation and time-slot length to maximize energy efficiency; RIS phase shift is closed-form Eq. (2), GT order comes from ACO (pp. 5-8).
system: Single AAV serves N ground terminals by OFDMA (2 MHz, K subchannels); 10x10 reflecting RIS on a building wall; antennas, carrier frequency not stated (pp. 3-4, 10).
method: Deep RL: ACDRL (DQN with ACO scheduling), HDCDRL (Q network plus policy network for hybrid actions), T-DRL (copy networks, fine-tune); reinforcement learning with transfer fine-tuning (pp. 6-9).
data_channel: Custom simulator: LoS-probability air-to-ground model (Eq. 4) and RIS two-hop gain (Eq. 3); no 3GPP model, dataset or measurement; trained and tested on simulated GT layouts (pp. 4, 9-10).
test_conditions: Trained on one GT layout (Task1); tested on Task2 with a changed number and distribution of GTs, directly (Reuse) or after fine-tuning (T-DRL) (pp. 9, 12).
baselines: Learned: DQN, DDQN, DDPG (each with ACO scheduling and RIS) and Retrain/Reuse schemes; non-learned: ACO, GA, DFS only as GT-order schedulers compared on tour fitness; DQN-noRIS ablation (pp. 10-12).
metrics: Average reward, energy efficiency (CDF), fitness (inverse tour distance) and complexity cost of the GT-scheduling algorithms (pp. 9-11).
complexity: Table III gives orders only for GT-scheduling heuristics: DFS O(n!), GA O(g p n), ACO O(g n^2); none for the DRL networks (p. 11).
openness: none (no code or data link in the paper, pp. 1-13).
q1_support: p. 4: "The Los channel probability between AAV and the nth GT at time slot t can be expressed as in (4)". Custom simulator (LoS probability of [28], RIS gain of [27]); no 3GPP TR 38.901/38.811, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 12: "the number and distribution of GTs have changed somewhat between the new task and the old task"; also p. 12: "only fine-tuning training is needed". The Reuse and T-DRL schemes are tested on that new task (Fig. 9).
q3_support: p. 10: "DQN-noRIS: This scheme is a baseline scheme that ablates the RIS provisioning." Learned baselines exist (DQN, DDQN, DDPG, p. 10) but no non-learned method is compared on energy efficiency; ACO, GA, DFS are compared only as GT-order schedulers, p. 11: "we take the inverse of the distance sf as the fitness function for evaluation".
q4_support: p. 11: "the complexity cost of ACO and GA algorithms is at the polynomial level". Table III lists only DFS O(n!), GA O(g*p*n), ACO O(g*n^2) for the GT-scheduling heuristics; no parameters, FLOPs or runtime of the DRL networks (ACDRL, HDCDRL, T-DRL).
q5_support: p. 9: "The actual experimental environment is executed on Pycharm, the language environment is Python 3.7.1, and the training environment is Pytorch 1.9.0". Custom simulation (Table II, p. 10); no code or data link and no public channel dataset.
notes: Included as area 6: the DRL action holds the AAV move, time-slot length and subchannel assignment (p. 6), so a physical-layer decision (resource allocation in an aerial link) is learned jointly with one above it (trajectory), which Step 1 admits. RIS phase is closed-form Eq. (2) (p. 4) and GT order comes from ACO (p. 6), so area 3 does not apply. Borderline for the reviewer: above_phy (trajectory dominates; transmit energy neglected, p. 3), q3 (ACO/GA/DFS compared on tour fitness, not on energy efficiency), q4 (Table III covers only the non-learned ACO scheduling module of ACDRL, not the DRL part).
